title: AI SDRs & Hyper-Personalization
tagline: The guardrails behind an AI SDR: waterfall enrichment with a credit budget, signal-based personal hooks with a draft linter, and multi-step sequences that respect time zones, weekends and mailbox caps.
why: An AI SDR is only as good as its data and its brakes. Bad enrichment means bounced emails and burned domains. Generic hooks get ignored. A sequence that keeps emailing someone who replied, or sends 400 emails from one mailbox on a Monday, gets the domain blocked. This repo covers the deterministic parts that keep an AI SDR safe and relevant, before any LLM writes a word.
covers: Clay-style waterfall: providers in order, per-field first valid answer, stop when filled, credit budget, per-provider spend, fill rate
Email syntax check before accepting an enriched email
Hook selection by priority and freshness (funding, hiring, tech change, content), with a generic fallback
Template fill with {{variables}} and a lint gate: unresolved variables, word limit, spam words, exactly one CTA
Sequence builder: business-day waits, Monday-based weeks, local send hour to UTC, mailbox daily cap with overflow, stop on reply / bounce / unsubscribe
gaps: No Clay / Apollo / scraping connection: provider responses are synthetic JSON
No LLM call: the hook library is the place an LLM draft would plug in, and the linter is the gate it must pass
Does not send email and does not check deliverability (SPF, DKIM, warm-up)

ops.label: Waterfall enrich
ops.help: Fill email, title and headcount from cheap providers first. A bad email from one provider is skipped and the next provider is tried.

ops.label: Personalize + lint
ops.help: Pick the freshest high-priority signal as the hook, fill the template and lint the draft. Edit the body to see the linter fail.

ops.help: Schedule a 4-step sequence. Day 0 is a Monday. Weekends are skipped, the mailbox cap pushes overflow, and replied prospects get no steps.
